solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Page to introduce work by a philosopher

indicators.note: to introduce something is to come before it

explanation.surface: A publisher's page introduces a book written by some philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like it names the author of the work, but it supplies letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Popper, the Austrian-born thinker of 'The Open Society', is one example of a philosopher: a definition by example.

clue.text: Showed great disrespect for academic article backing study

indicators.note: to back is to move backwards, so the word for study is written in reverse

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: Someone snubbed a scholarly paper that supported a piece of research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic article' reads as one thing, a journal paper, and 'study' as research; the study here is a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To profane is to treat something sacred with irreverence or contempt, which is showing it great disrespect.

clue.text: Small hard seed, just the thing for bird

parts.note: a pip is a small hard seed, as in an apple
'it' = the very thing, as in 'that's it!'

explanation.surface: A tiny seed is the ideal feed for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the seed bird food, so the bird looks like the seed's consumer rather than the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small brown songbird of open country, related to wagtails.

clue.text: Loud sound perceived here could cause panic

parts.note: fear is what could cause panic
f = forte, loud; take it away from FEAR

explanation.surface: A loud noise heard here might spark a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: add loud (F) to the answer and you get FEAR, which could cause panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing happens in this organ on the side of the head, the place where sound gets picked up.

clue.text: Captain, man at sea for fish

parts.note: skip = skipper, a captain of a team
a jack (Jack Tar) is a sailor

explanation.surface: A ship's captain and a sailor go out to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIP is the sports captain (in curling or bowls), not a ship's master.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipjack is a small striped tuna, much of it canned; the name also covers some other leaping fish.

clue.text: Viceroy, the man to come down following king

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so the man and his descent go after the king

parts.note: to dive is to come down fast

explanation.surface: A viceroy tells a man to step down in favour of the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The Khedive was the Ottoman viceroy of Egypt, a word met mostly in crosswords and history books.
explanation.definitionFit: Khedive was the title of the ruler who governed Egypt on behalf of the Ottoman sultan from 1867 to 1914.

clue.text: Member of local community in city greeting one queen

explanation.surface: A local resident of some city says hello to a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In city' seems to place the community member; 'in' is only the link, and the city is the first chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A parishioner lives in, or worships in, a parish, the smallest local unit of church community.

clue.text: Notice archdeacon is grabbed by "dry" member of Christian sect

indicators.note: what is grabbed is held in the grabber's hands, so the little word sits inside the word for dry

explanation.surface: A notice says an archdeacon was seized by a teetotal member of a sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is grabbed' reads as a passive verb about the archdeacon; the 'is' is really the thing grabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventists, such as the Seventh-day Adventists, are a Protestant denomination awaiting Christ's second coming.

clue.text: Greek character, dissolute type cut up in physical combat

indicators.note: a word that is cut has lost a piece, here the last letter of the dissolute type
in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the whole is reversed

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man; cut, he loses his E

explanation.surface: A dissolute Greek gets carved up in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' looks like one phrase meaning upset or slashed; it is two instructions, one for the rake and one for the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art of unarmed fighting with strikes and kicks.

clue.text: Hint about bad person who has position in church ministry

definitions.text: who has position in church ministry
definitions.note: The definition is a relative clause; read it as 'one who has a position in church ministry'.

indicators.note: about means around, so the hint is wrapped round the bad person

parts.note: a cue is a hint or prompt
a rat is a nasty, treacherous person

explanation.surface: Someone drops hints about a villain holding a post in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad person' and the definition both describe people, so the break between wordplay and definition is easy to misplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant priest in an Anglican parish, holding an office in the church's ministry.

clue.text: Loves to keep very quiet with right music as appropriate

indicators.note: to keep is to hold on to, so the loves hold the quiet sign between them

parts.note: love = O, a nil score; two of them
a tune is a piece of music

explanation.surface: Lovers keep very quiet, with the right music, as is fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loves' is plural, so it gives two Os, and the pair of them make the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed or suited to the occasion, which is what appropriate means.

clue.text: Tour finally done with? Maybe not, for me

definitions.text: Tour finally done with? Maybe not, for me

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so take the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the tour is finally over, and answers: not for me.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, spoken by the answer: a wanderer's travels are never done.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue is a wanderer speaking: for a restless traveller the touring is never finished.

clue.text: Experts in things old and quaint, broadcast stars

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters of quaint are scattered

explanation.surface: Experts in quaint antiques appear on a TV show with stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old and quaint' looks like one phrase; the definition stops at 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiquaries are collectors and scholars of antiquities, relics and ancient history.

clue.text: Raving curtailed with police finally invading square in isolated position

indicators.note: curtailed literally means with the tail cut off, so the last letter goes
finally means at the end, so take the last letter of police

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a college square
raving = ranting; curtailed, it loses G

indicators.note: invaders get inside, so these letters go into the square

explanation.surface: A raving man is cut short when police finally storm a square.
explanation.walkthrough: The square is the container, though it comes last in the clue: its first three letters open the answer and its D closes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quarantined is kept in isolation to stop a disease spreading.

clue.text: Large cask put back in butt

indicators.note: to put something back is to send it backwards, so the cask is written in reverse

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A big barrel is stored inside a larger one.
explanation.walkthrough: A butt is a cask too, so the surface is all barrels; here 'butt' is the verb, to strike with the head.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to nut someone is to headbutt them.

clue.text: Make amends for former robber stifling resistance

indicators.note: to stifle a sound is to suppress it, so the resistance is silenced out of the robber

parts.note: a pirate is a robber at sea; lose R
r = resistance, in physics; the letter removed

explanation.surface: A reformed robber makes amends by no longer resisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stifling' looks like a container word, but the R is stifled out of existence, not held.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a sin or crime is to atone for it, paying a penalty or doing penance.

clue.text: Old man raised gun on island, a location in South America

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, and in a down entry going up reverses the gun

parts.note: gat = a gun, in gangster slang

explanation.surface: An old man raises his gun on an island somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'location' belongs to the wordplay, supplying the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the region at the southern tip of the continent, shared by Argentina and Chile.

clue.text: Anger about team suffering setback — no real cure, alas

indicators.note: about means around, so the anger goes round the team
a setback sends things backwards, so the whole assembly is reversed

parts.note: XI = eleven, a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: Someone is angry that the team has had a setback that nothing can cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alas' makes the definition fair: the answer promises a cure but, sadly, is no real one.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a supposed cure-all potion, the stuff of quacks, so it is regrettably no genuine remedy.

clue.text: Catholic stars promoting American star

indicators.note: to promote is to move up, and in a down entry up means to the top, so A goes first

parts.note: a = American; moved from the constellation to the top
Taurus, a constellation, without its A

explanation.surface: Catholic celebrities are promoting an American celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The A promoted is the one already in Taurus: write RC then TAURUS, and lift that A to the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcturus is the brightest star in the constellation Boötes, and one of the brightest in the night sky.

clue.text: A person like Macbeth, inadequate with first sign of death approaching

indicators.note: something inadequate falls short, so the word loses its last letter
the first sign of a word is its opening letter, here of death

parts.note: Macbeth was Thane of Glamis; THANE cut short

explanation.surface: A figure like Macbeth, not up to the job, with death drawing near.
explanation.walkthrough: A thane was a Scottish lord holding land from the king; Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and of Cawdor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at hand is near in time, about to happen, so it is approaching.

clue.text: Do "er" and "but" slip out when I speak?

definitions.text: Do "er" and "but" slip out when I speak?

indicators.note: letters that slip out of place are no longer in their given order

explanation.surface: A speaker wonders whether hesitations creep into their speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: someone unsure lets slip hesitant 'er's and 'but's.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue describes a sceptic whose speech is full of hesitation and objection, the words of someone unconvinced.

clue.text: Church showing love for one cruel person

indicators.note: for means in place of, so love takes the place of one in the church

parts.note: a minster is a large church
one = I, the Roman numeral; replaced by O

explanation.surface: A church shows love to a cruel person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing love for' reads as affection; 'for' is the swap, love standing in for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster, figuratively, is a person of inhuman wickedness or cruelty.

clue.text: Mum — one worshipped endlessly — became successful

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter of the worshipped one is dropped

parts.note: a deity is worshipped; without its end

explanation.surface: Mum, adored without end, has done well for herself.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'one worshipped endlessly' look like praise of Mum, adored for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: To make it is an idiom for achieving success, especially in a career.

clue.text: Country's hot spicy ingredients

definitions.meaning: the possessive of a South American country
the peppers, in one of their spellings

explanation.surface: A country's cooking uses hot, spicy ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords ignore apostrophes, so the country's possessive and the peppers' plural are one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile's belongs to the South American country; chiles is the American and Mexican spelling of chillies, hot peppers.

clue.text: I hate that putting husband first is sign of affection

indicators.note: putting means placing, so the husband's letter is moved to a new spot
first means at the front, where the husband's letter goes

parts.note: h = husband; moved to the front

explanation.surface: Someone who hates having the husband come first gets a hug anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation already contains the H; it just moves from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Embracing someone with your arms is a common physical gesture of fondness.

clue.text: He'd not blurt out shocking revelation

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, as in out of joint, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A discreet man would never blurt out a shocking secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blurt out' is a natural phrase, so 'out' hides inside it; the apostrophe in He'd is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a thunderbolt is a sudden, startling piece of news, a bolt from the blue.

clue.text: Animal sheltering in hot territory

indicators.note: something sheltering in a place is inside it, so the answer lies within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the gap, after the h of hot

explanation.surface: An animal takes cover in hot country.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is doing the sheltering in the surface, and in the wordplay it is the answer hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a fish-eating mammal of rivers and coasts, related to weasels.

clue.text: Famous Russian square fell finally in Revolution

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so take the last letter of fell
a revolution is a turning round, so the letters are reversed

explanation.surface: A famous square in Russia fell at last in the Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is a number, not a place such as Red Square, and the capital R of Revolution points at 1917, where the answer belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Lenin led the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 and founded the Soviet state.

clue.text: Academic session, end of year: this person's having examiner round

indicators.note: having means holding, joining the setter's pronoun onto the letter before
round means surrounding, so the examiner goes about the rest
the end of a word is its last letter, here of year

parts.note: this person is = I'm, the setter

explanation.surface: An academic term, at the end of the year, with an examiner sitting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person's' means 'this person is', the setter talking about themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is one of three terms dividing the academic year, especially in American universities.

clue.text: What restricts movement ultimately in old character

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the query word hems in a letter
ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter of movement

explanation.surface: What ultimately holds back movement, in an old person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' is not a question word introducing the clue; it is the query itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Eth is a letter used in Old English and still in Icelandic, written ð, a character of an ancient alphabet.

clue.text: Criterion to remain in force — difficult for Cockney to follow

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so the Cockney's word goes after the first piece

parts.note: a rule stands, remains in force

explanation.surface: A rule to remain in force proves hard for a Londoner to keep up with.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their Hs, so hard loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a benchmark or level of quality by which things are judged.

clue.text: Beginning of spring with cross-country runners — they churn up the soil

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of spring

parts.note: in hare and hounds, the hares are the runners laying the trail

explanation.surface: At the start of spring, cross-country runners churn up the muddy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The runners in the surface seem to be the ones churning up the soil; the definition means ploughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares, short for ploughshares, are the blades of a plough that cut and turn the earth.
